why_the_gap: The breakeven bucket disappeared. His pre-server journal recap reported three categories - '25 trades, 22 Wins, 3 BE, 0 loss' (msg 2, 2026-05-06). Every server-era summary reports only Trades / Wins / Losses (msgs 315, 848). With 10 breakeven positions in the reconstruction, folding that bucket into wins alone moves the headline by several points, and it is the single cleanest explanation of the gap.

Ambiguous outcomes are resolved at his discretion, sometimes literally by vote: 'Just checking because I don't know if I should count it as a win or loss as it went to huge profits, I'll pick what the majority says' (msg 403).

The loss count is understated in both published months - 9 claimed vs 13 reconstructed in May, 5 claimed vs 7 reconstructed in July. Losses are the denominator-sensitive term; two missing losses in a 45-trade month is worth about 4 points of win rate.

Whole categories of trade are declared unofficial BEFORE the fact and therefore cannot lose: gold and oil ('I won't count gold trades in crypto summary', msg 405), 5m entries ('Just an idea won't count TP or SL, not an official trade', msg 135), coins he posts but is not personally taking (msg 317), and late-month setups ('Not an official setup, had 40+ setups this month gonna chill rn', msg 843).

Not every trade reaches the server. He concedes it directly: 'I post all my trades in this server but since I wanna grow my X too some of my personal or once in a while trades will be there' (msg 877). Any reconstruction from Discord alone is therefore a subset, and the missing subset is self-selected.

Position-count limits and post-target coasting filter the sample upstream of the tally. He declines setups he rates highly because too many are open (msgs 24, 48, 187, 706), closes trades purely for clutter (msg 769), and stops posting after a good run ('My weekly goal has been done, so I'll take it slow until next week', msg 875). Clutter closures land in the manual-close bucket, which contains no losses.

The reconstruction and his tally are not counting quite the same universe. His May count of 60 exceeds the 54 positions recoverable from the channel; his July count of 45 is one fewer than the 46 recoverable. The two figures drift in opposite directions, which is what you would expect from a hand-kept tally rather than from a systematic bias in the reconstruction.

None of the above requires bad faith, and the reconstruction does not support a fraud reading. It supports a narrower one: the trading is better than average and the bookkeeping is generous, informal, and always generous in the same direction.

how_he_wins.mechanic: Discretionary early exit - he can always choose to book, and he only chooses when green
how_he_wins.explanation: This is the structural fact that produces the win rate. He does not usually leave a resting take-profit; he closes manually when he sees a rejection, a wick, a stall, or simply wants the slot. Because the decision to close is his and the decision to lose is the stop's, discretionary exits are one-directional: they convert unrealised green into a recorded win and never into a recorded loss. Losses can only arrive the one way he cannot veto - through a stop. The cost is that he leaves the tail of every winner on the table, which is exactly why his average R is small.
how_he_wins.numbers: Exit types across 217 positions: manual_close 62, take_profit 45, stop_loss 35, breakeven 11, unknown 43. Of the 62 manual closes, 61 are wins, 1 is breakeven, 0 are losses. All 35 losses closed at a stop. Only 45 of 120 wins (38%) reached a target he had published; at least 26 wins were manual closes booked short of the stated TP. There are more manual closes than take-profits.
